title: Tesla Targets 1 Million Optimus Robots a Year by Late 2027
summary:
CEO Elon Musk says the company intends to scale the output of its humanoid robots to approximately 20,000 units per week within the next 12 months. Tesla has installed most of the capacity for 1 million units of annual production at its Fremont plant, though Musk described the initial growth phase as a "shallow slope" of an S curve. The company forecasts that deliveries to customers outside of Tesla will begin in late 2027.

Musk noted that the robot's artificial intelligence, reliability and electromechanical design still require refinement, targets he expects to meet by the end of next year. This scaling effort follows the recent start of production-quality Optimus output on high-volume lines in California. To support future expansion, Tesla is also constructing a second dedicated robotics facility in Texas.

selectedTweets.text:
Tesla says they have officially started Optimus production in Fremont on their high-volume lines.

"The bots coming off this line are the first production quality bots that we have manufactured. While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product."

selectedTweets.text:
Elon Musk on Optimus:

"We've started early production. The growth of Optimus is an S curve, but the initial curve is a shallow slope. We have the vast majority of the 1 million unit/year line installed at Fremont. There's still some things we need to tweak about the design. There's still quite a lot of work to do with the AI in the robot. I would expect that the AI, the electromechanical design, reliability, usage life, expect these issues to be solved by the end of next year. I remain convinced Optimus will be the biggest product on Earth. I do want to temper expectations that we still have a lot to get through, it will take about a year to get through that."

TESLA CONFIRMS OPTIMUS HUMANOID ROBOT PRODUCTION HAS BEGUN

$TSLA says its first production-quality Optimus robots are now coming off high-volume manufacturing lines at its Fremont, California factory.

Tesla says its manufacturing process is now suitable for a commercial product, although hardware improvements will continue.

Production remains in the early ramp stage, while its Texas facility is still under construction.

Tesla has not disclosed production volumes or a timeline for full-scale manufacturing.
